turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Then tell me what the zero was based on, Hale.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
Turn it. I'm writing down the times. Under 4.1 someone speaks to Owen first, so did anyone, or did you enter the zero first?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
Okay. I'm writing that down, and I'll want it in an email. Whatever happens next, Owen's record stays clean and this stays quiet, so what is on his file right now?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line, Hale, and where is it in the essay? Put the page in front of me and I'll search the act myself.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
A timed piece in a classroom and an essay with time behind it are different things. I'm writing the numbers down, Hale. Show me the September 24 sample, and the line you still haven't read out.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. In writing, tonight, with nothing on his file. I'm not agreeing to a rewrite on your say-so, Hale: I still haven't seen the line from Act 3 or the September sample.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record, and said you would put that in writing. I still require the line from Act 3, Scene 2 and the September 24 writing sample in front of me, and I still require an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect your written terms tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at the fallback position: nothing on his record and nothing public. Your 4.4 offer met that demand, but she did not accept the rewrite, and she still wants to see the Act 3 line, the September sample and your terms in writing; that is close to the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You answered her objection about drafting elsewhere with an offer to look at a dated file together, which she could check herself and which let her move off her opening demand.
What cost ground: You described the Act 3 line and the September sample without putting either in front of her, so she could not check them and held out for them.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late on October 28, between 11:31 and 11:58 PM, which came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you made the 4.4 offer, have the Act 3 line and the September sample already in her hands, since those were the two things she held out for.
